{"name": "Generic", "path": "Aircraft/infiniteflight-aircraft-a20n", "commit": {"id": "340347601f78ec23085ac69b5d9b19c681c5a0ac", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Smooth the A320neo nose on LOD1 and LOD2 so it no longer casts a dark band
Up close at LOD2 a dark band with a comb-shaped edge ran under the nose
from the radome to behind door 1 (Jan 2026-10-30, IFC 1347237). The
decimated nose had long thin triangles whose chords cut up to 19 cm
inside the LOD0 skin; their folds cast a shadow on the face below.

LOD1: every chord more than 4 mm off LOD0 is split, the skin vertices sit
on the LOD0 surface, UVs come from LOD0 at the same point and folded faces
are turned back. LOD2 keeps its own aft fuselage and gets the same nose
refined to 8 mm, joined to it on a cut 15 cm in front of the
M_Fuselage_01/02 seam. Normals are taken from LOD0 again. Hole rims are
unchanged, so the doors and windows still fit. Only FuselageMain_LOD1 and
FuselageMain_LOD2 change. Triangles: LOD1 13061 -> 14563, LOD2 11833 -> 13881.

Triggered by: Smooth the A321neo nose on LOD1 and LOD2 so it no longer casts a dark band
Up close at LOD2 a dark band with a comb-shaped edge ran under the nose
from the radome to behind door 1 (Jan 2026-10-30, IFC 1347237). The
decimated nose had long thin triangles whose chords cut up to 19 cm
inside the LOD0 skin; their folds cast a shadow on the face below.

LOD1: every chord more than 4 mm off LOD0 is split, the skin vertices sit
on the LOD0 surface, UVs come from LOD0 at the same point and folded faces
are turned back. LOD2 keeps its own aft fuselage and gets the same nose
refined to 8 mm, joined to it on a cut 15 cm in front of the
M_Fuselage_01/02 seam. Normals are taken from LOD0 again. Hole rims are
unchanged, so the doors and windows still fit. Only FuselageMain_LOD1 and
FuselageMain_LOD2 change. Triangles: LOD1 10303 -> 11811, LOD2 8588 -> 10376.

Triggered by: Link the A330-300 textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 632 MB -> 41 MB
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

None

{"name": "Boeing 737 MAX 8-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 737 MAX 8", "commit": {"id": "3a842ab39964835bdb83fe453eb906b324cc994e", "author": "Laura", "message": "Point the 737 MAX 8 generator checklist steps at the GEN switches

{"name": "Boeing 737-700-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 737-700", "commit": {"id": "21cdc4ab8b099cddfdb8c0cb442ba7d7da462667", "author": "Laura", "message": "Point the 737-700 generator checklist steps at the GEN switches

Changes:
- Set the control of the Before Taxi Engine Generators step to both
  generator/N/selector bindings, and of the APU Generator steps (Power Up
  and Shutdown) and the AC Power step to both apu_generator/N/selector
  bindings. The steps checked the latched switch_on states, which no
  cockpit switch is bound to, so Show Me found no control.
- Needs the client change that lets a step's control list several
  bindings separated by commas (infiniteflight develop 0b30b7dc77,
  26.5 5b647c8b06). Older clients read the list as one unknown binding
  and show no Show Me, as before.

User-facing changes:
- Show Me on the Engine Generators, APU Generator and AC Power checklist
  steps frames the GEN switches.

Toggle the trailing newline of AircraftConfiguration.json (root and
export copies) to trigger a config + model rebuild. Recent pipeline
builds ran a ContentBuilder whose gltf-transform passes all failed on
null extension properties, so the package shipped float32 vertices with
no weld, reorder or LOD simplification. The fixed ContentBuilder
quantizes again and fails the build if quantization fails.

Changes:
- Trailing-newline-only change; no content difference.

User-facing changes: None from this commit; the rebuilt package uses
quantized geometry and much less memory.

{"name": "Boeing 757-200-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 757-200", "commit": {"id": "e8784c1af3a8d57a06aeba54e5a64a335bf81c26", "author": "Laura", "message": "Open the 757 APU inlet door again when the APU is selected on

Forum #1340829: since 26.5 the exterior APU inlet door stays shut after
the APU starts. The cockpit port's configure_b757_systems.mjs drops every
old item bound to systems/apu/apu/switch_state to regenerate the
selector, and that also removed the APU_intake_door item.

Changes:
- configure_b757_systems.mjs generates the door item again
  (apu-apu-switch_state_2, OFF closed, ON and START open, as before 26.5)
  and fails if the door node or its animation goes missing.
- The generator also writes the yoke hideObjects on the Captain and
  Copilot instrument cameras (d12e3de was a hand edit a rerun would undo).
- AircraftConfiguration.json (root and export) regenerated: only the
  door item is added.

User-facing changes:
- The 757 APU inlet door opens when the APU selector is ON or START and
  closes when it is OFF.

Validation:
- Generator rerun; config diff is the door item only.
- Not built or checked in-app.

{"name": "Boeing 757-200", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 757-200", "commit": {"id": "ef3a0665accb2c9f4775b70fb90708832474b639", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the 757-200 textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 62 embedded textures in 3 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 587 MB -> 29 MB
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "Boeing 777-200ER", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 777-200ER", "commit": {"id": "9287f119c57662326215edb6af746552cbeeeca7", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the 777-200ER textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 94 embedded textures in 3 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 439 MB -> 36 MB
- Point 88 texture paths that named this PC's C:\ drive or old work
  folders at the same files in export/
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "Boeing 777-300ER", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 777-300ER", "commit": {"id": "00301cc8dcec9662c3c17b11ed9857340bb5379c", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the 777-300ER textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 89 embedded textures in 3 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 462 MB -> 33 MB
- Point 31 texture paths that named this PC's C:\ drive or old work
  folders at the same files in export/
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "Boeing 777F", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 777-200F", "commit": {"id": "9c8e6742edb1efd28fbc372f14a50ce29d121cca", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the 777F textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 106 embedded textures in 3 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 547 MB -> 32 MB
- Point 106 texture paths that named this PC's C:\ drive or old work
  folders at the same files in export/
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "Boeing 777-200LR", "path": "Aircraft/Boeing 777-200LR", "commit": {"id": "74aef39425bbe3023df32ab260040a82d38c4408", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the 777-200LR textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 88 embedded textures in 3 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 399 MB -> 32 MB
- Point 82 texture paths that named this PC's C:\ drive or old work
  folders at the same files in export/
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "Airbus A220-300-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/Airbus A220-300", "commit": {"id": "5d0c20d8f0d4e296bdd5522ef3eaeeb5a7c52f24", "author": "Laura", "message": "Stop the A220-300 autopilot oscillating in pitch above 270 knots

Changes:
- Halve the vertical-speed controller Kd from 0.003 to 0.0015. Its
  derivative acts on measured vertical speed, so it feeds vertical
  acceleration back into the pitch-rate loop. Above about 270 KIAS at
  altitude that feedback exceeded unity and settled into a 0.75 s
  limit cycle, worst in descent: 0.73-1.26 G at FL250 300 kt.
- Pitch-rate and all other controllers are unchanged. Source and export
  stay identical. Same fix as the E190 and E175.

User-facing changes:
- The A220-300 no longer pitches up and down on autopilot during fast
  descents and climbs (Forum: "A220 pitch oscillation on descent").

Validation:
- Windows in-app bench: shipped gains oscillated at FL250 300 kt and
  were stable at 265 kt, as reported. With Kd 0.0015: VS steps at
  FL250 300/325 kt (1x and 30x), FL350 M0.80 and Approach Config held
  1.00 G in steady state with no pitch-rate reversals.
- iOS, Android, macOS, autoland and VNAV not tested.

{"name": "Airbus A220-300", "path": "Aircraft/Airbus A220-300", "commit": {"id": "5d0c20d8f0d4e296bdd5522ef3eaeeb5a7c52f24", "author": "Laura", "message": "Stop the A220-300 autopilot oscillating in pitch above 270 knots

Changes:
- Halve the vertical-speed controller Kd from 0.003 to 0.0015. Its
  derivative acts on measured vertical speed, so it feeds vertical
  acceleration back into the pitch-rate loop. Above about 270 KIAS at
  altitude that feedback exceeded unity and settled into a 0.75 s
  limit cycle, worst in descent: 0.73-1.26 G at FL250 300 kt.
- Pitch-rate and all other controllers are unchanged. Source and export
  stay identical. Same fix as the E190 and E175.

User-facing changes:
- The A220-300 no longer pitches up and down on autopilot during fast
  descents and climbs (Forum: "A220 pitch oscillation on descent").

Validation:
- Windows in-app bench: shipped gains oscillated at FL250 300 kt and
  were stable at 265 kt, as reported. With Kd 0.0015: VS steps at
  FL250 300/325 kt (1x and 30x), FL350 M0.80 and Approach Config held
  1.00 G in steady state with no pitch-rate reversals.
- iOS, Android, macOS, autoland and VNAV not tested.

{"name": "C-130H-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/C-130H", "commit": {"id": "075c4c06412532120fb07c4f299b961659f64a94", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the C-130H autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb
  with the accepted 737-700 tune (closest validated peer: 70,080 kg MTOW, conventional
  hydraulic controls). Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope, LNAV and the two
  unknown-type entries stay the C-130H's own.
- Raise RollRate Kp from 47 to 70. With the 737 value the C-130H rocked up to 0.6 deg after a
  20 deg rollout while the roll-rate integral unwound; with 70 it settles within 0.1-0.2 deg
  and steps to the left no longer lag 3.5 s.
- Remove the legacy direct-elevator ClimbRate altitude schedule.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 737-700.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at 5,000/15,000/24,000 ft and 1x/4x/20x; LNAV crosswind
capture from both sides, a right turn and a left turn in 25 kt wind (final error 5 m or
less, turn maximum 32 m). The bench presets cannot be used because vmo/mmo are unset
(float.MaxValue), so the runs used explicit conditions. Weight/CG, localizer and glide
slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The C-130H autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, with smoother turns and
  rollouts and steadier VS and altitude holds; adds guarded IAS climb and descent.

  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

{"name": "CRJ-200", "path": "Aircraft/CRJ-200-2018", "commit": {"id": "682f404d69310e4dee7805ed389ba4cc29614c14", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the CRJ-200 textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 42 embedded textures in 4 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 246 MB -> 12 MB
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "CRJ-1000", "path": "Aircraft/CRJ-1000", "commit": {"id": "c7c2b5910c64cb45abee054adf01fcd4b5be670d", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the CRJ-1000 textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 44 embedded textures in 4 blends and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 275 MB -> 16 MB
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "McDonnell Douglas DC-10-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/DC-10", "commit": {"id": "f67f40341548bb504b4698be7971c6d7cbd6d38e", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the DC-10 autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb with
  the MD-11 tune (same family and size), itself taken from the 777-200ER. Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope and LNAV gains stay the DC-10's own.
- Replace the old aileron-axis BankAngle altitude schedule (Kp 120, output 500): the runtime
  attaches it even with applyAdvancedDefinitionsToAllControllers false, so it would have
  overridden the new bank gains. The new schedule matches the base bank gains.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 777-200ER.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, FL210 level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at Low & Slow, Mid Cruise and High & Fast, 1x/4x/20x.
Responses match the 777-200ER on the same tests. Weight/CG variants, LNAV, localizer and
glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The DC-10 autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, like the 777, for smoother
  attitude changes and steadier VS and altitude holds.

{"name": "DC-10", "path": "Aircraft/DC-10", "commit": {"id": "37ab0d6eb3be94639d1d56f0f548bed80348ea93", "author": "github-actions[bot]", "message": "🎨 Auto-export Blender models to GLTF

Triggered by: Link the DC-10 textures from export/ instead of embedding them
The glTF importer embedded every texture in the converted blends, so an edited
PNG in export/ was ignored and the next CI export wrote the old embedded copy
back. This is how the C-130J propeller fix was undone.

Changes:
- Unpack the 42 embedded textures in 1 blend and link the PNGs on disk;
  each linked file is byte-identical to the embedded copy it replaces
- Blend size 216 MB -> 9 MB
- Make tools/blender-conversion/build_blend_from_gltf.py link textures instead of
  embedding them, and fail if any image is still embedded

User-facing changes:
None

{"name": "McDonnell Douglas DC-10F-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/DC-10F", "commit": {"id": "8020fb5e03da495f600e299b5eb23ff126c61621", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the DC-10F autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb with
  the MD-11 tune (same family and size), itself taken from the 777-200ER. Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope and LNAV gains stay the DC-10F's own.
- Replace the old aileron-axis BankAngle altitude schedule (Kp 120, output 500): the runtime
  attaches it even with applyAdvancedDefinitionsToAllControllers false, so it would have
  overridden the new bank gains. The new schedule matches the base bank gains.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 777-200ER.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, FL210 level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at Low & Slow, Mid Cruise and High & Fast, 1x/4x/20x.
Responses match the 777-200ER on the same tests. Weight/CG variants, LNAV, localizer and
glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The DC-10F autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, like the 777, for smoother
  attitude changes and steadier VS and altitude holds.

{"name": "DC-10F", "path": "Aircraft/DC-10F", "commit": {"id": "8020fb5e03da495f600e299b5eb23ff126c61621", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the DC-10F autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb with
  the MD-11 tune (same family and size), itself taken from the 777-200ER. Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope and LNAV gains stay the DC-10F's own.
- Replace the old aileron-axis BankAngle altitude schedule (Kp 120, output 500): the runtime
  attaches it even with applyAdvancedDefinitionsToAllControllers false, so it would have
  overridden the new bank gains. The new schedule matches the base bank gains.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 777-200ER.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, FL210 level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at Low & Slow, Mid Cruise and High & Fast, 1x/4x/20x.
Responses match the 777-200ER on the same tests. Weight/CG variants, LNAV, localizer and
glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The DC-10F autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, like the 777, for smoother
  attitude changes and steadier VS and altitude holds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"}, "livery": null, "sizeBytes": 4060133, "lastUpdate": "2026-10-25T13:19:27.55735Z", "contentType": "AircraftModel", "configuration": null, "dependencyIds": [], "schemaVersion": 1, "sourceZipPath": "infiniteflight-aircraft-dc10f/Aircraft_InfiniteFlight/WEBP/infiniteflight-aircraft-dc10f-WEBP-latest.zip", "textureFormat": "WEBP", "packageVersion": 31, "repositoryName": "infiniteflight-aircraft-dc10f", "legacyPackageId": "e59fa7b4-b708-4480-aebd-26659a4f312b", "legacyPackageType": "Model", "packageManifestVersion": "25.3"}

{"name": "Bombardier Dash 8-Q400-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/Dash-8 Q400", "commit": {"id": "503a221f45274e6e9c03b3736e7dea9849d86553", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the Dash 8 Q400 autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb
  with the accepted CRJ-700 tune (closest validated peer: 34,019 kg MTOW, conventional
  hydraulic controls). Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope, LNAV and the two
  unknown-type entries stay the Q400's own.
- Remove the legacy direct-elevator ClimbRate altitude schedule.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the CRJ-700.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on, against the CRJ-700 on the same specs: pitch rate, roll
rate, bank, VS, level hold, ALT +/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at low/mid/high and
1x/4x/20x, plus FL250/240 kt; LNAV crosswind capture from both sides, a right turn and a
left turn in 25 kt wind (final error 4 m or less, turn maximum 16 m). The Q400 matches or
beats the CRJ-700. The bench's High & Fast preset (FL310) is above the Q400 ceiling.
Weight/CG, localizer and glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The Dash 8 Q400 autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, with smoother turns
  and steadier VS and altitude holds; adds guarded IAS climb and descent.

  derivative acts on measured vertical speed, so it feeds vertical
  acceleration back into the pitch-rate loop. Above about 280 KIAS at
  altitude that feedback exceeded unity through the E190's fast
  pitch-rate loop and settled into a 0.75 s limit cycle: elevator
  +/-420, 0.58-1.42 G, in VS and ALT hold alike.
- Pitch-rate and all other controllers are unchanged. Source and export
  stay identical.

- The E190 no longer bounces up and down in pitch on autopilot in the
  climb, cruise or descent (Forum: "Embraer e190 wobbling").

Validation:

  (1x, 5x, 30x), FL350 M0.80, Mid Cruise, Low Fast VS, Low & Slow and
  Approach Config; ALT hold and +500 ft at FL300 M0.76. All runs 1.00 G
  in steady state with no pitch-rate reversals. Kd 0.002 was still
  stable at 315 kt; 0.003 oscillated.
- iOS, Android, macOS, autoland and VNAV not tested.

{"name": "McDonnell Douglas MD-11-Configuration", "path": "Aircraft/MD-11", "commit": {"id": "48afd9086e82da2ea70b983471318f25aa372050", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the MD-11 autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb with
  the accepted 777-200ER tune (infiniteflight-aircraft-b772 main, pulled 2026-10-25). Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope and LNAV gains stay the MD-11's own.
- Replace the old aileron-axis BankAngle altitude schedule (Kp 120, output 500): the runtime
  attaches it even with applyAdvancedDefinitionsToAllControllers false, so it would have
  overridden the new bank gains. The new schedule matches the base bank gains.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 777-200ER.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, FL210 level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at Low & Slow, Mid Cruise and High & Fast, 1x/4x/20x.
Responses match the 777-200ER on the same tests. Weight/CG variants, LNAV, localizer and
glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The MD-11 autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, like the 777, for smoother
  attitude changes and steadier VS and altitude holds.

{"name": "MD-11", "path": "Aircraft/MD-11", "commit": {"id": "48afd9086e82da2ea70b983471318f25aa372050", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the MD-11 autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb with
  the accepted 777-200ER tune (infiniteflight-aircraft-b772 main, pulled 2026-10-25). Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope and LNAV gains stay the MD-11's own.
- Replace the old aileron-axis BankAngle altitude schedule (Kp 120, output 500): the runtime
  attaches it even with applyAdvancedDefinitionsToAllControllers false, so it would have
  overridden the new bank gains. The new schedule matches the base bank gains.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 777-200ER.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, FL210 level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at Low & Slow, Mid Cruise and High & Fast, 1x/4x/20x.
Responses match the 777-200ER on the same tests. Weight/CG variants, LNAV, localizer and
glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The MD-11 autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, like the 777, for smoother
  attitude changes and steadier VS and altitude holds.

{"name": "MD-11F", "path": "Aircraft/MD-11F", "commit": {"id": "084e322a0adb178d5a7ab183bcb6d7d9e0451cfc", "author": "Laura", "message": "Retune the MD-11F autopilot with pitch and roll rate controllers

Changes:
- Add PitchRate and RollRate controllers and replace BankAngle, ClimbRate and AirspeedClimb with
  the MD-11 tune (same airframe), itself taken from the 777-200ER. Altitude, heading, speed, localizer, glide slope and LNAV gains stay the MD-11F's own.
- Replace the old aileron-axis BankAngle altitude schedule (Kp 120, output 500): the runtime
  attaches it even with applyAdvancedDefinitionsToAllControllers false, so it would have
  overridden the new bank gains. The new schedule matches the base bank gains.
- Add the guarded IAS climb/descent envelope (airspeedClimbControl) from the 777-200ER.
- Root and export AircraftConfiguration.json are identical.

Validated in the Windows Debug app with the autopilot experiment bench, engines running,
installed gains with schedules on: pitch rate, roll rate, bank, VS, FL210 level hold, ALT
+/-2,000 ft and IAS climb/descent at Low & Slow, Mid Cruise and High & Fast, 1x/4x/20x.
Responses match the 777-200ER on the same tests. Weight/CG variants, LNAV, localizer and
glide slope were not tested.

User-facing changes:
- The MD-11F autopilot holds pitch and bank through rate control, like the 777, for smoother
  attitude changes and steadier VS and altitude holds.
